author: Wang Xiangwei
description:
Before boarding my flight to Boston late last month, I spent the better part of three days doing something I never imagined I would do in more than 30 years of covering China: scrubbing my phone. Old emails, screenshots, WeChat threads that might be read the wrong way, anything that could be misconstrued in an airport interview room – all deleted, just in case.
I was not being paranoid. I was following advice now routinely passed among Chinese travellers to the United States: carry a clean...
title: Heading to America to bridge the gap in US-China relations

author: Alcott Wei
description:
Radically rewriting world and Chinese history without solid proof could threaten China’s international image and national identity, a leading Communist Party journal has warned.
There has been a growing trend to promote a less Western-centric view of history in recent years, while Beijing has also been keen to promote the idea that Chinese civilisation has a long and continuous history.
But at the same time, the so-called pseudo-historical school – which has cast doubt on the origins of Western...
title: Rewriting world history puts China’s image and ‘cultural security’ at risk: party journal

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
China is rapidly expanding a flight-test facility deep in its western desert, satellite imagery has revealed, a push that analysts say could help fast track the development of its next-generation military aircraft as air-power rivalry with the United States intensifies.
Latest satellite photos of the facility near Lop Nur, in China’s western Xinjiang region, show four large new hangars, new taxiway work, a circular pad believed to be an engine-run or turnaround area, and possible fuel-storage...
title: What China’s Lop Nur desert base expansion means for PLA stealth jets in race with US

author: Jane Cai
description:
China has been urged to draw on the lessons from Ukraine’s communications as it looks at new forms of wartime messaging.
A recent study concluded that in the complex modern information environment, possessing advanced technology was not enough because success would depend on “weaving” together the information strategy and military operations.
It said such campaigns should try to shatter the adversary’s sense of security while strengthening domestic resolve and gathering international...
title: Why China is being urged to study Ukraine’s wartime PR blitz in the AI age

author: Holly Chik
description:
China will thwart US ambitions for global artificial intelligence (AI) dominance, the vice-president of the Centre for China and Globalisation has said, while warning that Washington’s military-focused strategy was pushing towards “AI for evil”.
Addressing the Penang Peace Dialogue in Malaysia on Sunday, Victor Gao said the US was “weaponising and militarising AI”, and integrating the technology into systems ranging from drones and ballistic missiles to everyday software and hardware.
This drive...
title: China will never allow any country in this world to achieve AI dominance: Victor Gao

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A study in one of the world’s top scientific journals that concluded China’s policy-driven solar energy expansion was harming bird diversity has come under fire after allegations emerged that the analysis may have used observations of 2.1 billion little egrets in a single park – more than the entire global population of the species.
It also brought up heated conversations on social media about negative narratives surrounding China’s green energy sector.
The study in question – by researchers in...
title: Study that argued China’s solar policy hurt birds may have miscounted 2 billion egrets

author: Zhang Tong
description:
China is using the world’s most powerful geostationary weather satellite to track severe thunderstorms over Nepal and deliver real-time intelligence as the two countries continue search and rescue operations following last month’s devastating glacier collapse.
The Fengyun‑4C satellite – launched in December 2025 and now positioned 36,000km (22,000 miles) above the equator – carries a Lightning Mapping Imager (LMI) that captures 500 frames per second, sifting through 30 gigabits of data every...
title: World’s most powerful lightning-chasing satellite joins China-Nepal flood relief efforts

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China’s military researchers have proposed a redesigned “AI principles and practice course” for graduate students with “educating for war” at its centre, embedding combat scenarios to better prepare future officers for intelligent warfare.
Researchers from the National University of Defence Technology’s College of Intelligence Science and Technology outlined their proposal in the July issue of the journal Defence Industry Conversion in China.
The initiative comes as China seeks to cultivate more...
title: Chinese military university urged to revise AI course to ‘educate for war’

author: Zhang Tong
description:
China has launched a world-first industrial-scale facility to extract iron from previously discarded mine tailings and ultra-low-grade ore, turning waste into a valuable resource that can reduce its dependency on overseas supply.
According to the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) last Tuesday, a production line capable of processing 5.56 million tonnes of refractory iron ore and tailings per year has passed official checks and is now running steadily.
China is the world’s largest iron ore user,...
title: China begins mining iron from tailings, low-grade ore that can meet its demand for decades
